title: Study of ordering in (MoCrTi)$_{100-x}$Al$_x$ refractory high-entropy alloys using machine learning interatomic potential
authors: Jiyao Zhang, Klemens Lechner, Markus Maßwohl, Petra Spoerk-Erdely, David Holec
abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys have emerged as promising candidates for high-temperature applications due to their exceptional mechanical properties. Understanding the thermodynamic mechanisms underlying chemical ordering in these complex systems is critical for optimizing their performance. In this work, by utilizing a universal machine learning interatomic potential with hybrid Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations, the temperature-dependent thermodynamics and mechanical properties of (MoCrTi)(100-x)Alx system have been investigated. The heat capacities and short-range order parameters reveal distinct order-disorder transition behaviors. While the Mo25Cr25Ti25Al25 and Mo32Cr32Ti32Al4 alloys exhibit a single transition dominated by the synergistic ordering of B2-type atomic pairs, the Mo28Cr28Ti28Al16 and Mo30Cr30Ti30Al10 alloys display two separate transitions: a low-temperature stage driven by specific pairs (Mo-Al in Mo28Cr28Ti28Al16; Al-Al in Mo30Cr30Ti30Al10) and a high-temperature stage governed by the remaining pairs. Structural analysis indicates that in the low-temperature ordered B2 phase, Mo and Al share one sublattice while Cr and Ti share the other. Furthermore, the relationship between ordering and mechanical stiffness has been identified. Ordering significantly enhances the elastic constants and moduli, and gives rise to a non-monotonic compositional dependence. Unlike random solid solutions, where stiffness increases monotonically with decreasing Al content, ordered configurations exhibit a non-monotonic trend, peaking at the Mo30Cr30Ti30Al10 alloy. This enhancement is attributed to an optimized population of stiff atomic pairs induced by strong short-range order. These findings provide fundamental insights into the interplay between compositions, chemical ordering, and mechanical performance, offering guidance for the design of refractory high-entropy alloys.
summary: This work investigates how chemical ordering affects the properties of refractory high-entropy alloys using sophisticated simulations powered by machine learning interatomic potentials. The study reveals that compositional changes lead to distinct order-disorder transitions and that structural ordering significantly boosts mechanical stiffness, peaking at a specific composition ($	ext{Al}_{10}$). This provides fundamental design rules for developing robust high-temperature materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the thermodynamic mechanisms governing chemical ordering in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) to optimize their performance for high-temperature applications.
main_result: Chemical ordering significantly enhances the elastic constants and moduli of these alloys, exhibiting a non-monotonic dependence that peaks at specific compositions due to optimized stiff atomic pairs.
method: The research employs hybrid Monte Carlo (MC) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations utilizing a universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (uMLIP).
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{(MoCrTi)}_{100-x}	ext{Al}_x$ refractory high-entropy alloy. The modeling relies on advanced computational techniques, including uMLIPs and simulations tracking structural evolution.
key_observables: Heat capacities ($C_V$), Short-Range Order (SRO) parameters (Warren-Cowley), elastic constants ($C_{11}, C_{12}, C_{44}$), and bulk/shear moduli.
important_parameters: Al concentration ($x$) ranging from 0 to 0.25; Temperature ($T$); Pair stiffness ($k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the mechanical response is strongly coupled with the degree of chemical ordering, and calculations are performed using uMLIP potentials.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow diagram of MC/MD simulations; $C_V$ vs. Temperature profiles show distinct single or bimodal transition behaviors across compositions; elastic moduli plots demonstrate the non-monotonic peak in stiffness at $	ext{Al}_{10}$.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure detailing the simulation workflow (MC equilibration, NPT MD), analyzing thermodynamic transitions via $C_V$ and SRO parameters, and finally correlating these ordering states with measurable mechanical properties.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter alloys, the methodology heavily relies on advanced machine learning potentials (uMLIPs) to model complex many-body interactions in disordered systems, which is a key theme in ML-physics.
